entries.reason: SwiftUI and Swift Charts keep their requirements private (`_makeView`, `_body`, `_resolve`), so no app can adopt them, compiled or not. The built-in styles all work.
On iPhone a `Table` collapses to its first column with no headers, so it's a `List` that's harder to write; use a `List` of rows, or a `Grid` for columns.
It hands the app `NSItemProvider`s from a drag, which arrive with drag and drop (§4.1).
SwiftUI calls its static `height(in:)` while it lays out the sheet, off the main actor, where Kiln's code can't run; `.fraction(_:)` and `.height(_:)` cover the same sizes.
iOS has no `ScrollInputKind` to pass it: its kinds are watchOS's and visionOS's.
They'd call the app's code on the audio thread, many times a second; `AVAudioPlayer` plays `Data` the app makes (§3.5).

entries.what: Custom text renderers, animations and visual-effect types (`TextRenderer`, `customAttribute`, `CustomAnimation`, your own `VisualEffect`)
entries.reason: SwiftUI calls them on its render thread every frame, where an app's code can't run. `contentTransition(.numericText())`, `phaseAnimator`, `keyframeAnimator`, `Canvas` and `visualEffect`'s closure cover the effects.
They constrain a `TextEditor`'s `AttributedString` with attribute-scope types the app declares, which Kiln can't make native.
A `Chart` already describes itself to VoiceOver; a custom descriptor needs `AXChartDescriptor` types Kiln doesn't bridge.

entries.what: Opening the app from a URL or Handoff (`onOpenURL`, `userActivity`, `onContinueUserActivity`)
entries.reason: A Shelf app has no URL scheme or activity types of its own: the system routes those to Shelf.
Shelf owns the home indicator, whose swipe closes the app; and each app has one settings store, which `@AppStorage` already uses.
Kiln's `Float` is a `Double`: the same arithmetic and results an app relies on, printed with a `Double`'s digits (`Float.pi` prints 3.141592653589793, not 3.1415925).
A slice (`xs[2...]`) is a new array in Kiln, indexed from 0; compiled code keeps the base's indices. `Array(xs[2...])` is the same in both.

entries.what: Module names and Objective-C descriptions in printed values
entries.reason: An app has no module in Kiln: an enum in a printed array is `[s]`, where compiled code prints `[App.Size.s]`; `JSONSerialization`'s arrays print as Swift's, not `NSArray`'s.
Kiln writes keys sorted; compiled code writes a struct's in declaration order (and a dictionary's in hash order). The JSON means the same.
An app's code runs on the main actor, so waiting would freeze it: they return at once. `DispatchGroup.notify` and `async`/`await` wait without blocking.
`publisher(for:)` with `.onReceive`, and `addObserver(forName:object:queue:using:)`, cover it.
It customizes `DocumentGroup`'s document browser; a Shelf app is one screen, not a document-based app. The file pickers open and save files (§4.1).
It takes a Foundation `#Predicate`, which the compiler builds from a macro that Kiln doesn't expand. `allowedContentTypes:` filters what the picker offers.
They create and post to the person's iCloud Shared Albums through `PHPhotoLibrary`, which a Shelf app can't read: it can only add photos (§4.2).
